correctness.rationale: On the source affine chart the six Hessenberg equations are reconstructed directly from \(g^{-1}Ng\). After restricting to the named Schubert cell, exhaustive exact symbolic computation shows every maximal minor of the Jacobian is divisible by \(\Delta=z_{12}-z_{23}-z_{45}+z_{56}\) and one maximal minor is exactly \(\pm\Delta\). A \(5\times5\) minor is identically \(1\). Since the radical local ideal has codimension \(6\), the Jacobian criterion gives rank \(6\) exactly off \(\Delta=0\) and rank \(5\) exactly on \(\Delta=0\). The bundled verifier replays these identities and explicit test points.

value.rationale: The source uses this cell specifically to demonstrate that a singular permutation flag can lie in a generically smooth Hessenberg–Schubert cell. Determining the entire singular subset of that named counterexample is therefore a natural classification question, not an arbitrary slice. The result shows the exceptional set is a smooth affine hyperplane of non-permutation singular points with uniform Jacobian corank \(1\), sharply replacing a one-sided generic-smoothness test by an exact criterion and resolving the source prose/calculation discrepancy.
